title: Variant traffic blackhole caused by weight translation bug in rollout service
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-27 at ~14:07 UTC a subset of canary rollouts observed a sudden drop in requests routed to active variants. Approximately 18-32% of traffic for affected rollouts was routed to a non-existent backend path (blackhole) for ~42 minutes across multiple clusters. This manifested as elevated 5xxs and partial feature regressions for internal customers using canary traffic.

Scope and impact:
- Affected: 7 canary rollouts across two regions (us-west1, eu-west1).
- User-visible: internal dashboards and a small set of customer integrations saw elevated error rates; no data loss.
- Duration: 2026-02-27 14:07 UTC -> 2026-02-27 14:49 UTC (mitigation engaged) with follow-up rollbacks until 15:05 UTC.
- Root cause summary: A rounding/translation bug in the rollout weight translator component converted float weights into scaled integer weights incorrectly when weights were below 0.5%. The translator clamped and rounded these tiny weights to zero in certain code paths, producing stale route entries that pointed to removed variant backends. This produced intermittent blackholes when the proxy used cached route tables.

Detection and triage notes:
- First signal: automated SLO alert for increased 5xx rate on canary-tagged routes and a rise in per-route latency.
- Pager duty: alerted at 14:12 UTC. Oncall confirmed correlated spikes with recent rollout promotions.
- Initial mitigation: immediately paused new rollouts and triggered an emergency rollback for the most affected rollouts.

Links to artifacts and telemetry:
- Grafana incident panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rollouts/rollout-health?from=2026-02-27T13:30:00Z&to=2026-02-27T16:00:00Z
- Slack channel: #incident-rollouts (thread ts: 1677483642.000200)
- GitHub PR with fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/4728
- Post-incident dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rollouts/postmortem-53814
- Archived timeline notes: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/RND/ENG-53814+postmortem
comments: 2026-02-27 14:15 - Rafael Ortiz: Investigating routing tables and route translator diffs. Noticed weight->int translation module changed in last deployment (orchestrator v2026.02.4)
2026-02-27 14:28 - Dev: Emergency rollback applied to rollout IDs [rlt-7732, rlt-7740]. Partial recovery seen in us-west1 within 4m.
2026-02-27 14:49 - Ops: Global pause on new promotions enforced; background reconciliation job restarted to flush stale route cache entries.
2026-03-01 09:12 - QA: Reproduced weight rounding behavior in staging with synthetic traffic. Edge-case occurs when float weight < 0.005 and population of variants > 8.
2026-03-05 11:03 - Product: Noted customer concern from partner X; coordinating postmortem summary and outreach.
2026-03-09 16:50 - Security: No evidence of malicious activity; code regression confirmed.
root_cause: A recent change to the rollout weight translator introduced a non-linear quantization step intended to normalize tiny weights. The algorithm applied a clamp-and-round-to-percent optimization that mapped weights below 0.5% to zero in the exporter path, while the proxy cache expected the raw float-derived weight. The mismatch between exporter and runtime routing logic, compounded by cached route tables that were not invalidated fast enough, caused traffic to be directed to stale entries that no longer had active backends.
mitigation:
Immediate: paused new promotions, rolled back the most affected rollouts, and restarted the route reconciliation worker to flush caches. Medium-term fix: revert the clamp-and-round optimization and deploy a corrected translation that preserves sub-percent fractional weights. Deployed hotfix PR #4728 to or chestrator, followed by staged rollout to canaries then global.

Additional ops steps: add fast-cache-invalidation hook to rollout promotion path and a safety check that aborts promotion when exporter-proxy weight diffs exceed 0.1%.
